citations.assessment: The elder addresses Shimon ben Elazar in the first wine incident. There is a separate elder occurrence in the later incident.
Tosafot reports the universal identification in the name of some interpreters and then rejects its application in the next cited incident.
The exact death is on 34a. The elder with two myrtle branches on 33b is a distinct occurrence, as is the explicitly named Elijah at the cave.
The exact teaching is in 5b:3 in the checked edition. Keep Heilprin’s 6b as the reported locator and identify the verified locus.
The elder addresses Rav Yirmeyah bar Abba about the timing of the Shema. The following printed see-there is the same local pointer.
The elder’s full saying includes neither early nor late, but Heilprin excerpted only the early side. Preserve that selective quote.
The elder answers Abbahu’s instruction about scraping a shoe with a teaching of Ḥiyya.
Zeira remained silent when the elder first questioned him about a root aligned with an opening.
The elder addresses the Sabbath-honoring Yosef after the pearl episode.
The elder addresses Rav Yirmeyah in the discussion of fuel costs. Preserve Heilprin’s distinct honorific.
The exact approval concerns Yirmeyah’s exposition and is separately ascribed to Yoḥanan.
The checked witness offers Rabbah bar bar Ḥanah as the alternative speaker, and names Yoḥanan subsequently. Heilprin excerpts the elder reading.
The elder answers Rabbah bar Ulla and supports Ulla.
The elder teaches Ilfa using a case of weekly allowances for sons.
The anonymous elder tells Abaye the greater person has the greater inclination.
Elazar questions the elder about whether the remarriage permission followed immediately or after twelve months.
The elder’s objection to Rava’s public teaching is at the end of the chapter. Kiddushin independently preserves the parallel.
The old man reads the defective spelling as an instruction to conceal the divine name.
Shemuel reports the distinct lineage presumptions in Sava’s name. The juxtaposition supplies no warrant to identify him with the preceding elder.
In both alternative contexts the elder cites Rava’s public lecture on the high priests’ duty to pray for their generation.
The elder transmits the school of Shimon ben Yoḥai to two sages discussing Jerusalem’s gateway. The received text gives Rav Ḥanina and Rav Hoshaya, beside Heilprin’s titles and spellings.
The parallel to Gittin shows Eliezer bracketed against Elazar. Preserve Heilprin’s locally ambiguous abbreviation and received translation with this note.
The elder explains Yoḥanan to Ammi in the discussion of a miscarriage.
The elder identifies the Sages of the baraita with R. Eliezer in Yoḥanan’s name.
The elder tells Yirmeyah where Yoḥanan started the discussion of rejected offerings.
The quoted reading matches 12a:7. The irregular printed side ה remains explicit.
Rashi explains the elder’s disagreement about the number of perutot in two selaim.
The pinned entry cites the same elder’s encounter with Yosef and the exact aphorism.

holds.reason: The catalogue collects a recurrent designation across distinct settings. The primary sources and Tosafot’s rejection do not establish common personal identity.
